newsitem.title: USA: Lakeshore, Don Was buy majority stake in Will Records.
newsitem.headline: Lakeshore, Don Was buy majority stake in Will Records.

text.p: Just weeks after signing a film and television production deal, Grammy Award-winning record producer Don Was and Lakeshore Entertainment are now buying a majority stake in Seattle-based Will Records.

"Don's experience and Lakeshore's financial strength should make a good combination," said Joni Sighvatsson, who along with Tom Rosenberg heads Lakeshore Entertainment, a motion picture production and distribution company.
Iceland native Sighvatsson, who sold his Propoganda music video company to Polygram in 1992, said Was and Lakeshore were spending several millions of dollars for their stake in Will.
Was, one of the most highly regarded record producers in the music industry has worked with The Rolling Stones, Bonnie Raitt, Willie Nelson, Bob Dylan and Elton John.

Winner of the Grammy Award for Producer of the Year in 1995, Was also earned an Emmy nomination for a documentary on prolific songwriter and Beach Boys founder Brian Wilson and is currently directing a short film, produced by Francis Ford Coppola, which incorporates bits of songs from his upcoming solo compact disc "Forever Is a Long, Long Time".
Sighvatsson said the venture will develop soundtracks to go along with movies that are to be produced under a first-look deal Lakeshore signed with Was weeks ago.
They will also seek to develop new acts. "We're looking to develop bands from the movies on our labels," he said in an interview.
"We don't want to compete with the Big Six labels and we don't plan to throw money on the same acts that everyone is trying to get," he said.
Under the three-year film deal, Was and Lakeshore are developing a film called "The Knockout Artist."
"Don will continue to do bigger stuff on his own," Sighvatsson said.
Will Records was formed by Skip Williamson in 1993 to launch the release of "Forked" the first album by Sage, his brother's band.

The acts signed to the label include "grandaddy," whose debut full-length "don't sock the tryer" will be released in early 1997, "Lucky Me", who have songs featured in the upcoming film "Johns" and Katies Dimples, whose debut full-length "Timbre" is executive produced by Was.

"I find it genuinely exciting to be involved in this venture, because I know it's just a matter of time before Will Records reaches a new plateau. It's a good feeling to know that I'll be there when it does," Was said in a release.
"We want to build this company more organically and rely on and provide creative operational and financial support to our artists."
